subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Chai: India's National Drink
description: A short lesson to help you apply Chai: India's National Drink.

hook.text: India grows more tea than almost anyone, yet chai—spiced milky tea—only became popular in the 1900s.

buildup.text: The British Tea Board promoted tea to Indian workers in the 1920s. People added milk, sugar, and spices.

discovery.text: Chai wallahs—street tea vendors—built an entire economy around tiny cups of boiled, spiced tea.

twist.text: Chai uses CTC tea (crush-tear-curl), a strong variety invented specifically for milk-based brewing.

climax.text: India now drinks over 80% of the tea it grows. Chai isn't just a drink—it's India's social glue.

punchline.text: British marketing, Indian spices. The world got chai.

quiz.question: What type of tea is used in traditional chai?

details.summary: Masala chai, tea brewed with milk and spices, became India's national drink in the 20th century, partly through aggressive marketing by the British-owned tea industry. Chaiwalas on every corner made it affordable and ubiquitous.
details.whyItMatters: India's transformation from a tea-growing colony into the world's largest tea-consuming nation shows how colonial commerce can create genuine cultural traditions.
takeaways: Masala chai became India's national drink in the 20th century
Chaiwalas make tea affordable and available on every corner
India is both a top producer and the largest consumer of tea

faq.question: How did chai become so popular in India?
faq.answer: The British-owned Indian Tea Association promoted cheap tea consumption to create domestic demand. They installed chaiwalas at railway stations and factories. Spices and milk were added to stretch small amounts of low-grade tea and suit Indian palates. The habit became deeply embedded in daily life.

faq.question: What spices are typically in masala chai?
faq.answer: The most common spices are cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, and black pepper. Recipes vary by region and family. Some add star anise, fennel, or nutmeg. The tea is typically strong Assam CTC brewed directly in milk and water with sugar. Every chaiwala has their own recipe.
